facts.source_fact: An installation has ceased operation when all regulated activities have permanently ceased.
The cessation date is the date on which the regulated activities were last carried out.
The operator must notify the regulator through METS when all regulated activities cease, even if the operator considers the cessation temporary.
The notification date is the later of one month after all regulated activities ceased or 31 December in the scheme year of cessation.
No cessation notification is required if the operator has applied to surrender the permit.
No cessation notification is required if all authorised regulated activities resume before the notification date.
The regulator may determine that cessation is permanent where not satisfied that the operator intends to resume regulated activities.
The regulator's assessment can consider whether regulated activities are technically capable of resuming without physical changes.
The regulator's assessment can consider whether the operator intends to retain technical capability for regulated activities to resume.
A cessation notification is distinct from a permit-surrender application.
facts.expected_handling: Do not equate cessation notification with surrender.
